title: Plugin Kit
summary: A typed plugin SDK and test harness for building versioned event-processing extensions.
intended_users: Open-source maintainers and application developers embedding third-party event processors.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: The plugin protocol compares in-process and isolated execution and defines compatibility and deprecation trade-offs.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: The committed alternatives table compares benefits, rejected costs, and the condition that triggers reconsideration.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Discovery, manifest validation, capability policy, lifecycle, and diagnostics use stable public interfaces.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: The reference host validates capabilities but does not provide operating-system process isolation.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Reject a plugin manifest using an unsupported future protocol version. Reject plugin initialization when a requested capability is forbidden by the host. Clean up completed lifecycle hooks after a later initialization hook fails.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: The reference host validates capabilities but does not provide operating-system process isolation. Package registry signature and publisher identity verification remain consumer responsibilities.

testing_strategy: Committed cross-boundary, negative, and boundary tests: test/compatibility.test.js, test/capability-policy.test.js, test/lifecycle-failure.test.js. Their presence does not establish that they pass in Finch static review.
security_threat: A plugin requests undeclared or host-forbidden access during initialization. Control: The host intersects manifest declarations with an explicit host allowlist before invoking lifecycle hooks. A partially initialized plugin leaves earlier resources active after a later hook fails. Control: The host records completed hooks and invokes bounded reverse-order cleanup after initialization failure.
production_limitation: The reference host validates capabilities but does not provide operating-system process isolation. Package registry signature and publisher identity verification remain consumer responsibilities.
technical_debt: Complete deployment-specific runtime, performance, accessibility, and security evaluation before production use.
track_alignment_explanation: The project is a reusable, documented, licensed developer toolkit with a stable plugin surface and credible adoption path.
